parole.significato: A member of the Russian Airborne Troops.
parole.testo: From Russian десант (desant), from French descente (“descent”), in reference to parachuting. Doublet of descent.

Borrowed from Russian экранопла́н (ekranoplán), itself derived from экра́н (ekrán, “screen”) as used in экранный эффе́кт (ekrannyj effékt, “ground effect”), from French écran, + the root of French planer (“to glide, to hover”).

parole.significato: A meat patty or meatball made of ground pork and/or beef flattened into an oval shape, then seasoned and fried or baked.
parole.testo: From Russian котле́та (kotléta), from French côtelette (“cutlet; chop”), whence the English doublet cutlet; also a doublet of kotlet via Polish.

parole.significato: A type of ice cream made with vanilla, cream, eggs, and sugar.
parole.testo: From Russian пломби́р (plombír), from French plombières (“ice cream made with almond extract, kirsch, and candied fruit”), possibly after the commune of Plombières-les-Bains.

parole.significato: A card game, related to bridge, Boston, and whist.
parole.testo: From Russian префера́нс (preferáns), in turn from French préférence. Doublet of preference.

parole.significato: An administrative unit of some Eastern European and Asian states.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Russian райо́н (rajón), from French rayon. More recently influenced by the same name used in other post-Soviet states. Compare Ukrainian райо́н (rajón).

parole.significato: A small sausage made from a mixture of ground meats, spices, and sometimes other ingredients like breadcrumbs or grains.
parole.testo: From Russian соси́ска (sosíska), from French saucisse (“sausage (hot dog style)”) (whence English saucisse) + Russian -ка (-ka, diminutive suffix), from Old French saucice (whence English sausage).

parole.significato: The way in which the story is told throughout a book or film; an employment of narrative.
parole.testo: From Russian сюже́т (sjužét), from French sujet, from Latin subiectum.

Ultimately a calque of Russian ультралевый (ulʹtralevyj, “ultraleft”, adjective), in the sense of "pertaining to extreme or uncompromising leftist ideology." From ультра- (ulʹtra-, “ultra; extremely”) + левый (levyj, “left”, adjective), equivalent to ultra- + left. Originally applied pejoratively by
